- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce overshoot by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is falling, avoid premature bottoming — delay downward adjustment by 1–2 periods.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), reduce subsequent forecast by 5–10% to account for mean reversion.  
- If sentiment is mixed (0.25–0.75) and forecast diverges from recent 5-day average, align forecast toward 5-day moving average to reduce lag bias.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >10% increase from 10-day avg), reduce forecast peak by 5–8% to avoid horizon overfitting.
